prompt: By default, how does EIGRP determine the metric of a route for the routing table?

options.label: A
options.text: It uses the bandwidth and delay values of the path to calculate the route metric.

options.label: B
options.text: It uses a default metric of 10 for all routes that are learned by the router.

options.label: C
options.text: It counts the number of hops between the receiving and destination routers and uses that value as the metric.

options.label: D
options.text: It uses a reference bandwidth and the actual bandwidth of the connected link to calculate the route metric.

prompt: Refer to the exhibit. Which path is used by the router for Internet traffic?
When OSPF learns multiple paths to a network, how does it select a route?

options.label: A
options.text: For each existing interface, it adds the metric from the source router to the destination to calculate the route with the lowest bandwidth.

options.label: B
options.text: It counts the number of hops between the source router and the destination to determine the route with the lowest metric.

options.label: C
options.text: It divides a reference bandwidth of 100 Mbps by the actual bandwidth of the exiting interface to calculate the route with the lowest cost.

options.label: D
options.text: It multiplies the active K values by 256 to calculate the route with the lowest metric.

prompt: When a floating static route is configured, which action ensures that the backup route is used when the primary route fails?

options.label: B
options.text: The default-information originate command must be configured for the route to be installed into the routing table.

options.label: C
options.text: The floating static route must have a lower administrative distance than the primary route so it is used as a backup.

options.label: D
options.text: The floating static route must have a higher administrative distance than the primary route so it is used as a backup
